body.name: Positive binary separation models and catalogue
body.construction: In each model let \(U_X,U_A,U_B,U_C\) be mutually independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) bits and let \(E_Y,E_Z\) be mutually independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\varepsilon)\) bits independent of them. Model \(M_1\) has \(X=U_X\), \(Y=((1-X)U_A+XU_B)\oplus E_Y\), and \(Z=((1-X)U_B+XU_C)\oplus E_Z\). Model \(M_2\) has \(X=U_X\), \(Y=((1-X)U_A+XU_C)\oplus E_Y\), and \(Z=((1-X)U_B+XU_A)\oplus E_Z\). The catalogue is \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{sep}}=\{s,\chi_{Y,0},\chi_{Z,1},\rho_X,\rho_Y,\rho_Z\}\): \(s\) is a fresh SELECT; \(\chi_{Y,0}\) is CTF-RAND transmitting value zero from \(X\) only to child \(Y\); \(\chi_{Z,1}\) transmits value one only to child \(Z\); and \(\rho_v\) READs \(v\). SELECT precedes both CTF-RAND actions, which precede the READs; there are no conflicts. Set \(c_{\mathrm{sep}}(\chi_{Y,0})=c_{\mathrm{sep}}(\chi_{Z,1})=1\) and all other costs to zero. For each displayed legal protocol, \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\) returns the law generated by the displayed SCM equations and the exact binary support table; independent response noise makes every READ cell compatible with a fixed RAND or CTF-RAND label positive.
